verses.eng: "It came to pass then thereafter by command of the First Commandment that the great triple-powered Self-willed, who is one of the three triple-powers, pursued Sophia in the thirteenth aeon, in order that she should look towards the parts below, so that she might see in that region his lion-faced light-power and long after it and go to that region, so that her light might be taken from her.

Sophia takes the lion-faced power of Self-willed for the true Light. "It came to pass then thereafter that she looked below and saw his light-power in the parts below; and she knew not that it is that of the triple-powered Self-willed, but she thought that it came out of the light which she had seen from the beginning in the height, which came out of the veil of the Treasury of the Light. And she thought to herself: I will go into that region without my pair and take the light and thereout fashion for myself light-aeons, so that I may go to the Light of lights, which is in the Height of heights.

She descendeth to the twelve aeons and thence into the chaos. "This then thinking, she went forth from her own region, the thirteenth aeon, and went down to the twelve aeons. The rulers of the aeons pursued her and were enraged against her, because she had thought of grandeur. And she

went forth also from the twelve aeons, and came into the regions of the chaos and drew nigh to that lion-faced light-power to devour it. But all the material emanations of Self-willed surrounded her, and the great lion-faced light-power devoured The emanations of Self-willed squeeze the light-powers out of Sophia. all the light-powers in Sophia and cleaned out her light and devoured it, and her matter was thrust into the chaos; it became a lion-faced ruler in the chaos, of which one half is fire and the other darkness,--that is Yaldabaoth, of whom I have spoken to you many times. When then this befell, Sophia became very greatly exhausted, and that lion-faced light-power set to work to take away from Sophia all her light-powers, and all the material powers of Self-willed surrounded Sophia at the same time and pressed her sore.
"And Pistis Sophia cried out most exceedingly, she cried to the Light of lights which she had seen from the beginning, in which she had had faith, and uttered this repentance, saying thus:

The first repentance of Sophia. "'1. O Light of lights, in whom I have had faith from the beginning, hearken now then, O Light, to my repentance. Save me, O Light, for evil thoughts have entered into me. "'2. I gazed, O Light, into the lower parts and saw there an light. thinking: I will go to that region, in order that I may take that light. And I went and found myself in the darkness which is in the chaos below, and I could no more speed thence and go to my region, for I was sore pressed by all the emanations of Self-willed, and the lion-faced power took away my light in me. "'3. And I cried for help, but my voice has not reached out of the darkness. And I looked

to the height, that the Light, in which I had had faith, might help me. "'4. And when I looked to the height, I saw all the rulers of the aeons, how in their numbers they looked down on me and rejoiced over me, though I had done them no ill; but they hated me without a cause. And when the emanations of Self-willed saw the rulers of the aeons rejoicing over me, they knew that the rulers of the aeons would not come to my aid; and those emanations which sore pressed me with violence, took courage, and the light which I had not taken from them, they have taken from me. "'5. Now, therefore, O Light of Truth, you know that I have done this in my innocence, thinking that the lion-faced light-power belonged to you; and the sin which I have done is open before you. "'6. Suffer me no more to lack, O Adanay, for I have had faith in your light from the beginning; O Adanay, O Light of the powers, suffer me no more to lack my light. "'7. For because of your inducement and for the sake of your light am I fallen into this oppression, and shame has covered me. "'8. And because of the illusion of your light, I am become a stranger to my brethren, the invisibles, and to the great emanations of Barbelo. "'9. This has befallen me, O Light, because I have been zealous for your abode; and the wrath of Self-willed is come upon me--of him who had not hearkened to your command to emanate from the emanation of his power--because I was in his aeon without performing his mystery. "'10. And all the rulers of the aeons mocked me. "'11. And I was in that region, mourning and seeking after the light which I had seen in the height. "'12. And the guards of the gates of the aeons searched for me, and all who remain in their mystery mocked me. "'13. But I looked up to the height towards you and had faith in you. Now, therefore, O Light of lights, I am sore pressed in the darkness of chaos. If now you will come to save me,--great is your mercy,--then hear me in truth and save me. "'14. Save me out of the matter of this darkness, that I may not be submerged therein, that I may be saved from the emanations of god Self-willed which press me sore, and from their evil doings. "'15. Let not this darkness submerge me, and let not this lion-faced power entirely devour the whole of my power, and let not this chaos shroud my power. "'16. Hear me, O Light, for your grace is precious, and look down upon me according to the great mercy of your Light. "'17. Turn not your face from me, for I am exceedingly tormented. "'18. Haste you, hearken to me and save my power. "'19. Save me because of the rulers who hate me, for you know my sore oppression and my torment and the torment of my power which they have taken from me. They who have set me in all this evil are before you; deal with them according to your good pleasure. "'20. My power looked forth from the midst

of the chaos and from the midst of the darkness, and I waited for my pair, that he should come and fight for me, and he came not, and I looked that he should come and lend me power, and I found him not. "'21. And when I sought the light, they gave me darkness; and when I sought my power, they gave me matter. "'22. Now, therefore, O Light of lights, may the darkness and the matter which the emanations of Self-willed have brought upon me, be to them for a snare, and may they be ensnared therein, and recompense them and may they be made to stumble and not come into the region of their Self-willed. "'23. May they remain in the darkness and not behold the light; may they behold the chaos for ever, and let them not look to the height. "'24. Bring upon them their revenge, and may your judgment lay hold upon them. "'25. Let them not henceforth come into their region to their god Self-willed, and let not his emanations henceforth come into their regions; for their god is impious and self-willed, and he thought that he had done this evil of himself, not knowing that, had I not been brought low according to your command, he would not have had any authority over me. "'26. But when you had by your command brought me low, they pursued me the more, and their emanations added pain to my humiliation. "'27. And they have taken light-power from me and fallen again to pressing me sore, in order to take away all the light in me. Because of this in which they have set me, let them not

ascend to the thirteenth aeon, the region of Righteousness. "'28. But let them not be reckoned in the lot of those who purify themselves and the light, and let them not be reckoned with those who will quickly repent, that they may quickly receive mysteries in the Light. "'29. For they have taken my light from me, and my power has begun to cease in me and I am destitute of my light. "'30. Now, therefore, O Light, which is in you and is with me, I sing praises to your name, O Light, in glory. "'31. May my song of praise please you, O Light, as an excellent mystery, which leads to the gates of the Light, which they who shall repent will utter, and the light of which will purify them. "'32. Now, therefore, let all matters rejoice; seek you all the Light, that the power of the stars which is in you, may live. "'33. For the Light has heard the matters, nor will it leave any without having purified them. "'34. Let the souls and the matters praise the Adanay of all aeons, and [let] the matters and all that is in them praise him]. "'35. For God shall save their soul from all matters, and a city shall be prepared in the Light, and all the souls who are saved, will dwell in that city and will inherit it. "'36. And the soul of them who shall receive mysteries will abide in that region, and they who have received mysteries in its name will abide therein.'"
It came to pass then, when Jesus had spoken

these words to his disciples, that he said to them: "This is the song of praise which Pistis Sophia uttered in her first repentance, repenting of her sin, and reciting all which had befallen her. Now, therefore: 'Who has ears to hear, let him hear.'"

Marayam again came forward and said: "My Adanay, my indweller of light has ears, and I hear with my light-power, and your spirit which is with me, has sobered me. Hearken then that I may speak concerning the repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered, speaking of her sin and all that befell her. Your light-power has prophesied thereof aforetime through the prophet Dawad in the sixty-eighth Psalm:

Marayam interprets the first repentance from Psalm lxviii "'1. Save me, O God, for the waters are come in even to my soul. "'2. I sank, or am submerged, in the slime of the abyss, and power was not. I have gone-down into the depths of the sea; a tempest has submerged me. "'3. I have kept on crying; my throat is gone, my eyes faded, waiting patiently for God. "'4. They who hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head; mighty are my foes, who violently pursued me. They required of me that which I took not from them. "'5. God, you have known my foolishness, and my faults are not hid from you. "'6. Let not them that wait on you, O Adanay, Adanay of powers, be ashamed for my sake; let not those who seek you be ashamed for my sake, O Adanay, God of Israel, God of powers. "'7. For your sake have I endured shame; shame has covered my face. "'8. I am become a stranger to my brethren, a stranger to the sons of my mother. "'9. For the zeal of your house has consumed me; the revilings of them that revile you have fallen upon me. "'10. I bowed my soul with fasting, and it was turned to my reproach. "'11. I put on sackcloth; I became to them a bye-word. "'12. They who sit at the gates, chattered at me; and they who drink wine, harped about me. "'13. But I prayed with my soul to you, O Adanay; the time of your well-liking is [now], O God. In the fulness of your grace give ear to my salvation in truth. "'14. Save me out of this slime, that I sink not therein; let me be saved from them that hate me, and from the deep of waters. "'15. Let not a water-flood submerge me, let not the deep swallow me, let not a well close its mouth above me. "'16. Hear me, O Adanay, for your grace is good; according to the fulness of your compassion look down upon me. "'17. Turn not your face away from your servant, for I am oppressed. "'18. Hear me quickly, give heed to my soul and deliver it. "'19. Save me because of my foes, for you know my disgrace, my shame and my dishonour; all my oppressors are before you. "'20. My heart awaits disgrace and misery; I waited for him who should sorrow with me, but I could not come at him, and for him who should comfort me, and I found him not. "'21. They gave me gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. "'22. Let their table be to them for a trap and for a snare and for a retribution and for a stumbling-block. "'23. May you bend their backs at all time. "'24. Pour out your anger upon them, and let the wrath of your anger lay hold upon them. "'25. Let their encampment be desolate, let there be no dweller in their habitations. "'26. For they persecuted him whom you have smitten, and added to the smart of their woundings. "'27. They added iniquity to their iniquities; let them not come into your righteousness. "'28. Let them be wiped out of the book of the living, and let them not be written in among the righteous. "'29. I am a poor wretch who is broken too; it is the salvation of your face which has taken me to itself. "'30. I will praise the name of God in the ode, and exalt it in the song of thanksgiving. "'31. This shall please God better than a young bull which puts forth horns and hoofs. "'32. May the wretched see and make merry; seek you God, that your souls may live. "'33. For God has heard the wretched and despises not the prisoners. "'34. Let heaven and earth praise the Adanay, the sea and all that is therein. "'35. For God will save Tzayawan, and the cities of Judaea will be built up, and they will dwell there and inherit it. "'36. The seed of his servants shall possess it, and they who love his name shall dwell therein.'"

It came to pass then, when Marayam had finished speaking these words to Jesus in the midst of the disciples, that she said to him: "My Adanay, this is the solution of the mystery of the repentance of Pistis Sophia." It came to pass then, when Jesus had heard Marayam speak these words, that he said to her: Well said, Marayam, blessed one, the fulness, or blessed fulness, you who shall be sung of as blessed in all generations."

The second repentance of Sophia. Jesus continued again in the discourse and said: "Pistis Sophia again continued and still sang praises in a second repentance, saying thus: "'1. Light of lights, in whom I have had faith, leave me not in the darkness until the end of my time. "'2. Help me and save me through your mysteries; incline your ear to me and save me. "'3. May the power of your light save me and carry me to the higher aeons; for you will save me and lead me into the height of your aeons. "'4. Save me, O Light, from the hand of this lion-faced power and from the hands of the emanations of god Self-willed. "'5. For it is you, O Light, in whose light I have had faith and in whose light I have trusted from the beginning. "'6. And I have had faith in it from the time when it emanated me, and you yourself did make me to emanate; and I have had faith in your light from the beginning. "'7. And when I had faith in you, the rulers of the aeons mocked at me, saying: She has ceased in her mystery. You are my saviour and you are my deliverer and you are my mystery, O Light. "'8. My mouth was filled with glorifying, that I may tell of the mystery of your grandeur at all times. "'9. Now, therefore, O Light, leave me not in the chaos for the completion of my whole time; forsake me not, O Light. "'10. For all the emanations of Self-willed have taken from me my whole light-power and have surrounded me. They desired to take away my whole light from me utterly and have set an watch on my power, "'11. Saying one to another together: The Light has forsaken her, let us seize her and take away the whole light in her. "'12. Therefore then, O Light, cease not from me; turn you, O Light, and save me from the hands of the merciless. "'13. May they who would take away my power, fall down and become powerless. May they who would take away my light-power from me, be enwrapped in darkness and sink into powerlessness.'
"This then is the second repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered, singing praises to the Light."
It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished speaking these words to his disciples, that he said to them: "Do you understand in what manner I discourse with you?"
And Kayapaa started forward and said to Jesus:
Kayapaa complains of Marayam. "My Adanay, we will not endure this woman, for she takes the opportunity from us and has let none of us speak, but she discourses many times."

And Jesus answered and said to his disciples: "Let him in whom the power of his spirit shall seethe, so that he understands what I say, come forward and speak. But now, Kayapaa, I see your power in you, that it understands the solution of the mystery of the repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered. Now, therefore, Kayapaa, speak the thought of her repentance in the midst of your brethren."

Kayapaa interprets the second repentance from Psalm lxx. And Kayapaa answered and said to Jesus "O Adanay, give ear that I may speak the thought of her repentance, of which aforetime your power prophesied through the prophet Dawad, uttering her repentance in the seventieth Psalm: "'1. O God, my God, I have trusted in you, let me no more be put to shame for ever. "'2. Save me in your righteousness and set me free; incline your ear to me and save me. "'3. Be to me a strong God and a firm place to save me; for you are my strength and my refuge. "'4. My God, save me from the hand of the sinner and from the hand of the transgressor and from the impious one]. "'5. For you are my endurance, O Adanay, you are my hope from my youth up. "'6. I have trusted myself to you from my mother's womb; you have brought me out of my mother's womb. My remembrance is ever in you. "'7. I have become as the crazy for many; you are my help and my strength, you are my deliverer, O Adanay. "'8. My mouth was filled with glorifying, that I may praise the glory of your splendour the whole day long. "'9. Cast me not away in the time of age; if my soul fades, forsake me not. "'10. For mine enemies have spoken evil against me and they who lay in wait for my soul, have taken counsel against my soul, "'11. Saying together: God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him, for there is no saviour. "'13. Let them be ashamed and destroyed who calumniate my soul. Let them be enwrapped in shame and disgrace who seek evil against me.'
"This then is the solution of the second repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered."

Jesus promises to perfect the disciples in all things. The Saviour answered and said to Kayapaa: "Finely, Kayapaa; this is the solution of her. repentance. Blessed are you before all men on the earth, because I have revealed to you these mysteries. Aman, amen, I say to you: I will perfect you in all fulness from the mysteries of the interior to the mysteries of the exterior and fill you with the spirit, so that you shall be called 'spiritual, perfected in all fulness.' And, amen, amen, I say to you: I will give to you all the mysteries of all the regions of my Father and of all the regions of the First Mystery, so that he whom you shall admit on earth, shall be admitted into the Light of the height; and he whom you shall expel on earth, shall be expelled from the kingdom of my Father in the heaven. But hearken, therefore, and give ear attentively
to all the repentances which Pistis Sophia has uttered. She continued again and uttered the third repentance, saying:

The third repentance of Sophia. "'1. O Light of powers, give heed and save me. "'2. May they who would take away my light, lack and be in the darkness. May they who would take away my power, turn into chaos and be put to shame. "'3. May they turn quickly to darkness, who press me sore and say: We have become lords over her. "'4. May rather all those who seek the Light, rejoice and exult, and they who desire your mystery, say ever: May the mystery be exalted. "'5. Save me then now, O Light, for I lacked my light, which they have taken away, and I needed my power, which they have taken from me. You then, O Light, you are my saviour, and you are my deliverer, O Light. Save me quickly out of this chaos.'"

Marathaa asks and receives permission to speak. It came to pass then, before Jesus had finished speaking, that Marathaa came forward, fell down at his feet, kissed them, cried aloud and wept with lamentation and in humbleness, saying: "My Adanay, have mercy upon me and have compassion with me, and let me speak the solution of the repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered."

And Jesus gave his hand to Marathaa and said to her: Blessed is every one who humbles himself, for on him they shall have mercy. Now, therefore, Marathaa, are you blessed. But proclaim then the solution of the thought of the repentance of Pistis Sophia."

Marathaa interprets the third repentance from Psalm lxix. And Marathaa answered and said to Jesus in the midst of the disciples: Concerning the repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered, O my Adanay Jesus, of it your light-power in Dawad prophesied aforetime in the sixty-ninth Psalm, saying: "'2. Let them be put to shame and con-founded who seek after my soul. "'3. May they turn straightway and be put to shame, who say to me: Ha, ha. "'4. May all who seek you, be joyful and exult because of you, and they who love your salvation, say ever: May God be exalted. "'5. But I am wretched, I am poor; O Adanay, help me. You are my helper and defence; O Adanay, delay not.'
"This then is the solution of the third repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered, singing praises to the height."
It came to pass then, when Jesus had heard Marathaa speak these words, that he said to her: Well said, Marathaa, and finely."

And Jesus continued again in the discourse and said to his disciples: "Pistis Sophia again continued in the fourth repentance, reciting it before she was oppressed a second time, in order that the lion-faced power and all the material emanations with it, which Self-willed
had sent into the chaos, might not take away her total light in her. She uttered then this repentance as follows:

The fourth repentance of Sophia. "'1. O Light, in whom I have trusted, give ear to my repentance, and let my voice reach to your dwelling-place. "'2. Turn not away your light-image from me, but have heed to me, if they oppress me; and save me quickly at the time when I shall cry to you. "'3. For my time is vanished like a breath and I am become matter. "'4. They have taken my light from me, and my power is dried up. I have forgotten my mystery which heretofore I was wont to accomplish. "'5. Because of the voice of the fear and the power of Self-willed my power is vanished. "'6. I am become as a demon apart, who dwells in matter and light is not in him, and I am become as a counterfeiting spirit, which is in a material body and light-power is not in it. "'7. And I am become as a decan who is alone in the air. "'8. The emanations of Self-willed have sore oppressed me, and my pair has said to himself: "'9. Instead of with light which was in her, they have filled her with chaos. I have devoured the sweat of my own matter and the anguish of the tears from the matter of my eyes, so that they who oppress me may not take the rest. "'10. All this has befallen me, O Light, by your commandment and your command, and it is your commandment that I am here. "'11. Your commandment has brought me down, and I am descended as a power of the chaos, and my power is numbed in me. "'12. But you, O Adanay, art Light eternal, and do visit them who are for ever oppressed. "'13. Now, therefore, O Light, arise and seek my power and the soul in me. Your commandment is accomplished, which you did decree for me in my afflictions. My time is come, that you should seek my power and my soul, and this is the time which you did decree to seek me. "'14. For your saviours have sought the power which is in my soul, because the number is completed, and in order that also its matter may be saved. "'15. And then at that time shall all the rulers of the material aeons be in fear of your light, and all the emanations of the thirteenth material aeon shall be in fear of the mystery of your light, so that the others may put on the purification of their light. "'16. For the Adanay will seek the power of your soul. He has revealed his mystery, "'17. So that he may regard the repentance of them who are in the regions below; and he has not disregarded their repentance. "'18. This is then that mystery which is become the type in respect of the race which shall be born; and the race which shall be born will sing praises to the height. "'19. For the Light has looked down from the height of its light. It will look down on the total matter, "'20. To hear the sighing of those in chains,
to loose the power of the souls whose power is bound,-- "'21. So that it may lay its name in the soul and its mystery in the power.'"

Yawachanan asks and receives permission to speak. It came to pass while Jesus spoke these words to his disciples, saying to them: "This is the fourth repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered; now, therefore, let him who understands, understand,"--it came to pass then, when Jesus had spoken these words, that Yawachanan came forward, adored the breast of Jesus and said to him: "My Adanay, give commandment to me also, and grant me to speak the solution of the fourth repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered."
Jesus said to Yawachanan: "I give you commandment, and I grant you to speak the solution of the repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered."
Yawachanan answered and said: "My Adanay and Saviour, concerning this repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered, your light-power which was in Dawad, has prophesied aforetime in the first Psalm:

Yawachanan interprets the repentance from Psalm ci. "'1. Adanay, give ear to my supplication and let my voice reach to you. "'2. Turn not away your face from me; incline your ear to me in the day when I am oppressed; quickly give ear to me on the day when I shall cry to you. "'3. For my days are vanished as smoke and my bones are parched as stone. "'4. I am scorched as the grass, and my heart is dried up; for I have forgotten to eat my bread. "'5. From the voice of my groaning my bones cleaved to my flesh. "'6. I am become as a pelican in the desert; I am become as a screech-owl in the house. "'7. I have passed the night watching; I am become as a sparrow alone on the roof. "'8. My enemies have reviled me all the day long, and they who honour me, have injured me. "'9. For I have eaten ashes instead of my bread and mixed my drink with tears, "'10. Because of your wrath and your rage; for you have lifted me up and cast me down. "'11. My days have declined as a shadow, and I am dried up as the grass, "'12. But you, O Adanay, you endure for ever, and your remembrance to the generation of generation[s]. "'13. Arise and have mercy upon Tzayawan, for the time is come to have mercy upon her; the proper time is come. "'14. Your servants have longed for her stones, and will take pity on her land. "'15. And the nations will have fear of the name of the Adanay, and the kings of the earth have fear of your sovereignty. "'16. For the Adanay will build up Tzayawan and reveal himself in his sovereignty. "17. He has regarded the prayer of the humble and has not despised their supplication. "'18. This shall be recorded for another generation, and the people who shall be created will praise the Adanay. "'19. Because he has looked down on his holy height; the Adanay has looked down from the heaven on the earth, "'20. To hear the sighing of those in chains, to loose the sons of those who are slain, "'21. To proclaim the name of the Adanay in Tzayawan and his praise in Yarawashalam.'
"This, my Adanay, is the solution of the mystery of the repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered."

Jesus commends Yawachanan. It came to pass then, when Yawachanan had finished speaking these words to Jesus in the midst of his disciples, that he said to him: Well said, Yawachanan, the Virgin, who shall rule in the kingdom of the Light."
